content:
The "local folder size" setting controls how many messages are downloaded. The default value is 25 and can be increased. You can find this in settings > account name > fetching mail.

The app will display "load up to 25 more" at the bottom of a mailbox while additional messages are available on the server. I'd recommend only downloading x number of recent messages, rather than your full mailbox

Developers recommend not increasing the value beyond 500. The app is known to have performance and stability issues when increased beyond this value. See their comments linked below.

https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/10373

You can also set the age of messages to sync, for example, messages from the last 2 months. This can be helpful for people with very large mailbox's.

Navigate to settings > account name > fetching mail > sync messages from:

content:
Yes, a pull down on the message view or tapping sync all mail / sync account in the side menu initiates an immediate download of all new messages.

Have you granted the app permission to run in the background and excluded it from any battery optimisation via Androids settings.

Can you verify the incoming server settings are correct. Navigate to settings > account name > fetching mail > incoming server. Tap next. It will test the connection.

Have you checked that sync (or Push) in enabled on your Inbox. https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/configure-push-email-thunderbird-android

Have you changed any settings that might have disabled sync such as Settings > general settings > network > background sync

Have you tried reinstalling the app, manually add the account and test with default settings applied. This would rule out any mis-configured settings.
